lead: A `NaN` a `float` expression produced carries the hardware's sign bit, and that bit is not the same on every leg of the matrix.
body: `sqrt(-1.0)` is negative where the SSE default `NaN` is and positive on aarch64, so anything reading it — `f64::total_cmp` above all — answers one way on linux-x86_64 and the other on macos-aarch64 while each looks right on its own. Fold every `NaN` to one before ordering, as `nvs_stdlib::ordering::ordered` does, and never assert on a `NaN`'s sign.
